findings.description: The loop bound changed from `j < keys_result->numkeys` (base) to `j <= keys_result->numkeys`, so it runs numkeys+1 times. (a) It writes slot_buffer[numkeys], one int past the malloc(sizeof(int)*numkeys) block -> heap overflow. (b) It reads keys_result->keys[numkeys], one past the last valid entry: for numkeys<6 that is a zeroed keysbuf slot (pos=0 -> argv[0], the command name), so `GET foo` in cluster mode hashes 'get' vs 'foo', mismatches, and returns CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT; preprocessCommand then sets CLIENT_READ_CROSS_SLOT and getNodeByQuery replies -CROSSSLOT for ordinary single-key commands. For numkeys>=6 keys[] is exactly numkeys long, so the read runs off the buffer (past keysbuf into the `keys` pointer field, giving a wild argv index).
findings.failureMode: Heap out-of-bounds write and read; every keyed command in cluster mode wrongly rejected with -CROSSSLOT; ASM migration tasks cancelled via getSlotFromCommand.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop in extractSlotFromKeysResult reads/writes past the end

findings.description: `toolbar.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor)` was changed to `rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor`. With `rightSkeletonAddressBar.leading == container.trailing` and its width `= container.width - 32`, the toolbar's leading is now `container.trailing + width - 32` while its trailing stays at `container.trailing`, i.e. a required negative width. When `isSwipingTabsEnabled` is true the address toolbar's constraints become unsatisfiable ("Unable to simultaneously satisfy constraints") and the address bar renders off-screen/collapsed; the base pinned leading to the left skeleton bar, which resolves to the container's leading edge.

findings.description: The diff replaces `namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.ServerExecutionTests;` with a block-scoped namespace. .editorconfig sets dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0161.severity = warning for *.cs (the test-file section does not relax it) and eng/targets/CSharp.Common.targets enables EnforceCodeStyleInBuild, while eng/common/tools.sh passes /warnaserror and TreatWarningsAsErrors=true by default, so building this project through build.sh/build.cmd (the E2E project is built whenever ContinuousIntegrationBuild != true) fails with error IDE0161. findings.description: The BUILD002 error condition gains `AND '$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1'`, so the check that a servicing build did not drop package references now only runs when the patch version is exactly 1. From 10.0.2 onward removing a `<Reference>` from a shipping package produces no error, contradicting docs/BuildErrors.md ("this error only appears in servicing builds, which should not change references"). The accompanying ValidateBaseline=false (baseline is still 9.0.0) suggests the polarity was meant to be `!=`, which would exclude the stale-baseline patch instead of every later patch.
findings.failureMode: Breaking package-reference removal ships in a servicing update without a build error
findings.title: BUILD002 servicing guard narrowed to patch version 1 only

findings.description: PreReleaseVersionLabel is set to 'servicing' (line 22) but the new conditional PreReleaseBrandingLabel block only covers alpha/preview/rc/rtm, so PreReleaseBrandingLabel evaluates to empty. Directory.Build.targets builds BrandingVersionSuffix/PackageBrandingVersion from it, so non-stabilized servicing builds produce e.g. "Microsoft .NET 10.0.1 Build servicing.25555.106" for the hosting bundle name instead of "... 10.0.1 Servicing Build ...". Upstream v10.0.1 includes the missing line: <PreReleaseBrandingLabel Condition="'$(PreReleaseVersionLabel)' == 'servicing'">Servicing</PreReleaseBrandingLabel>.
findings.failureMode: Installer/package branding strings drop the release-kind word
findings.title: No PreReleaseBrandingLabel for 'servicing' leaves branding empty

findings.description: `@Roles("TEAM_MEMBER")` is the lowest team role: RolesGuard's hasMinimumRole compares indexes in TEAM_ROLES = [OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER] with `checkedRoleIndex <= requiredRoleIndex`, so a plain MEMBER (index 2 <= 2) passes. Any team member can POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite and obtain a link that lets outsiders join the team, while the sibling org endpoint and the tRPC handler require ADMIN/OWNER. The new e2e case "should fail to create invite as non-admin member" expects 403 and will receive 200.
findings.failureMode: authorization gap: privilege escalation on new endpoint
findings.title: Invite endpoint guarded by TEAM_MEMBER, letting any member mint invite links

findings.description: Seven robj* are passed (HSETEX, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, newobj) but argc is 6, so newobj (the value) is never copied into the new argv. The propagated command is `HSETEX <key> KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 <field>`, which hsetexParseArgs rejects with an arity error. Verified live: the replica logged a wrong-number-of-arguments error for hsetex and kept the stale value while the master had the new one. Same failure on AOF reload. Fix: pass 7 as argc.
findings.failureMode: Every HINCRBYFLOAT propagates a malformed HSETEX; replicas and AOF reject it, permanently diverging from the master (data loss).
findings.title: rewriteClientCommandVector argc=6 drops the value arg from propagated HSETEX

findings.description: The base line was `hashTypeSet(c->db, o,c->argv[2]->ptr,new,HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL);`; the diff drops HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL. hashTypeSet then calls hfieldPersist/listpackExUpdateExpiry and removes the field's expiration. Verified live: HSET h1 f1 10; HPEXPIRE h1 20000 FIELDS 1 f1; HPTTL -> 19996; HINCRBYFLOAT h1 f1 2.5; HPTTL -> -1. This regresses the existing test "HINCRBYFLOAT - preserve expiration time of the field" (hash-field-expire.tcl:851) and inverts the PR's intent, since the replica keeps the TTL via KEEPTTL while the master loses it.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT on a field with a TTL silently clears that TTL on the master; the field never expires and master/replica diverge.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT now erases the field TTL on the master (HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL dropped)

findings.description: The diff removes `static` from addHashFieldToReply, but grep shows every call site is inside src/t_hash.c (lines 2605, 2621, 2685, 2810) and no header declares it. findings.failureMode: Compliance rule 7 violation; unnecessary global symbol with no prototype in any header.
findings.title: addHashFieldToReply de-staticized though only used in t_hash.c

findings.description: Seven robj* are passed but argc is 6, so the value (newobj) is dropped: HINCRBYFLOAT propagates `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field` with no value. Verified: AOF contains a 6-argument HSETEX, AOF load logs '== CRITICAL == ... wrong number of arguments for hsetex' (write lost), and a replica with propagation-error-behavior panic (tests/assets/default.conf setting) crashes with 'Guru Meditation: This replica panicked ... hsetex'.
findings.failureMode: Replica/AOF apply of malformed HSETEX: replica errors and loses the write (divergence); AOF load hits serverAssert on fake-client reply -> startup crash.
findings.title: rewriteClientCommandVector argc=6 drops the value argument of propagated HSETEX

findings.description: Base line was `hashTypeSet(...,HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL);`. Dropping HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL makes HINCRBYFLOAT discard the field TTL on the master. Verified live: HTTL is 100 before and -1 after HINCRBYFLOAT. Since the propagated command carries KEEPTTL, the replica keeps the TTL, so master and replica diverge; HINCRBY still keeps the TTL.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT on a hash field with TTL loses the expiration on the master, and diverges from the replica which keeps it via the KEEPTTL propagation.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT now clears the field TTL on the master (HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL dropped)

findings.description: The removed line `keyword_like_val = f"%{keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')}%".replace(r"\u", r"\\u")` converted the keyword into the \uXXXX form actually stored in workflow_runs.inputs/outputs (written with json.dumps default ensure_ascii=True). findings.description: escape_like_pattern() prefixes % / _ / \ with a backslash, but the new SQL declares ESCAPE '|'. Backslash is then just a literal character while % and _ stay wildcards: a search for "50%" becomes pattern %50\%% and matches only text containing "50\", returning no rows; a query containing '|' has its next char un-wildcarded, returning false positives. Reachable when IRIS is the vector store and IRIS_TEXT_INDEX is set to false (default true).
findings.failureMode: wrong query results on IRIS LIKE fallback search
findings.title: IRIS LIKE fallback declares ESCAPE '|' while the pattern is backslash-escaped

findings.description: `handleShowReaderModeAction` (reducer for `GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode`) sets `displayView: .readerModeLongPressAction` instead of `.readerMode` (base line: `displayView: .readerMode,`). BVC dispatches showReaderMode when the reader-mode toolbar button is tapped (ToolbarMiddleware:266) and on accessibilityPerformMagicTap; BVC's `handleDisplayActions` maps `.readerModeLongPressAction` to `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()` which adds the page to the reading list, so tapping the reader-mode button no longer enters/leaves reader view and instead saves the page to the reading list with an "Added to Reading List" toast.

It also breaks the existing unit test testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes: the mock ToolbarState has readerModeState nil, so isEnabled flips from false to true and `XCTAssertEqual(savedExtras.isPrivate, false)` (which receives isEnabled through ToolbarTelemetry's extras) now fails.

findings.description: Guard inverted: base was `(currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL) ? url : nil`, head is `(currentURL.isWebPage() || currentURL.isReaderModeURL) ? url : nil`. Reader-mode URLs are `http://localhost/reader-mode/page`, so isWebPage() is already true and the extra `|| isReaderModeURL` now lets the raw internal URL through instead of nil. With a page open in reader mode, tapping the tabs/menu/cancel button dispatches cancelEdit with that URL; AddressBarState.handleCancelEditAction stores it (`toolbarAction.url ?? state.url`) and LocationView renders `getSubdomainAndHost(from: url.absoluteString)`, so the address bar shows "localhost" instead of the site's domain until the next navigation.
findings.failureMode: Wrong URL displayed in address toolbar while reader mode is active
findings.title: cancelEditMode keeps internal reader-mode URL in address bar

findings.description: `for (int j = 0; j <= keys_result->numkeys; j++)` iterates one entry too far (base used `j < numkeys`). It reads keys[numkeys] (past the last valid key) and writes slot_buffer[numkeys] past the numkeys-sized allocation. Verified at runtime: cluster mode, `SET foo bar` returns "CROSSSLOT Keys in request don't hash to the same slot" (the extra entry has pos 0 => argv[0], the command name), and a 6-key `MGET {t}a..{t}f` reads keysbuf[6] which overlaps the `keys` pointer field, giving a huge pos and crashing the server (SIGSEGV in extractSlotFromKeysResult).
findings.failureMode: Heap out-of-bounds read/write; server crash and bogus CROSSSLOT rejection of every keyed command in cluster mode
findings.title: Off-by-one loop reads past keys array and writes past slot_buffer

This also violates the repo mandate to use zmalloc/zfree. Fix: use zmalloc/zfree (the same correction applies to all three sites).
findings.failureMode: Compilation failure of src/cluster.c; no binary produced
findings.title: malloc/free break the build (deprecated in server.h, -Werror)

findings.failureMode: Formatter check reports the file as unformatted.
findings.title: teamService.ts loses its trailing newline

findings.description: The @nestjs/common import is hand-wrapped although it fits within the 110-char line width; `biome format` reports it would collapse lines 9-17 (and the createInvite signature at 35-37) onto single lines, so the new file is not in the repository's mandated Biome format.

findings.failureMode: MODULE_NOT_FOUND at require time -> Ghost fails to boot
findings.title: members-api.js requires non-existent './lib/magic-link/magic-link'

findings.description: `config.get("bundle")` returns the bundle object, so the following `.as_str()` always yields None and `original_identifier` is always None. Mobile flows that call `ConfigMetadata::original_identifier()` (mobile/mod.rs) then fail with "app configuration is missing an identifier".
findings.failureMode: wrong key lookup makes value always None
findings.title: original_identifier now reads "bundle" instead of "identifier"

findings.description: `config_path.extension() == Some("json") && config_path.extension() == Some("json5")` can never hold for a single path, so the JSON-schema validation block is dead code; invalid tauri.conf.json no longer reports schema errors nor exits.
findings.failureMode: inverted/contradictory condition disables validation
findings.title: Schema validation gate changed from || to && (never true)

findings.description: The assignment `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value)...` was replaced by an extensions insert, so `value` is computed and discarded. Callers (mobile android_studio_script / ios xcode_script) that pass `--config` overrides keep the unmerged config; e.g. a devUrl override is ignored right after merge_with returns.
findings.failureMode: dropped side effect: merged config never stored
findings.title: merge_with no longer applies merged config to the loaded config

findings.description: New line is 156 characters while rustfmt.toml sets max_width = 100; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` reports the file as needing formatting, failing the mandated formatting check.
findings.failureMode: CI formatting check failure
findings.title: Line exceeds rustfmt max_width=100 (cargo fmt --check fails)

findings.description: Flipping "strict" to false breaks three required gates in .github/workflows/ui-v2-checks.yml. (1) Build job (`npm run build` = `tsc -b && vite build`): 242 TS errors, incl. TanStack Router's hard guard 'strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json'. (2) Lint job (`npm run lint`): 5 @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment errors, because useWatch<AutomationWizardSchema> degrades to `any` without strictNullChecks - this is what makes `posture` untyped in the four new components. (3) validate:types (`tsc -b --noEmit`). Restoring strict:true with all other PR code unchanged makes tsc AND eslint both exit 0, so the flip is unnecessary. Also violates AGENTS.md rule 11.
findings.failureMode: CI Build and Lint jobs fail; strict type checking disabled repo-wide.
findings.title: strict:false breaks CI Build, Lint and validate:types

findings.description: Line 36 hardcodes name="trigger.expect" while the sibling DeploymentStatusTriggerFields (same diff, line 31) and pre-existing FlowRunStateTriggerFields switch to trigger.after when posture is Proactive. Probe with identical user actions (select "Stays in", pick a status) shows WorkPool produces expect:["prefect.work-pool.paused"] with no `after`, while Deployment produces after:["prefect.deployment.ready"]. The posture label reads "Stays in", so the saved automation does not express the user's stated intent.
findings.failureMode: Selecting "Stays in" writes status to expect, leaving after undefined; wrong trigger payload.
findings.title: Work pool status field ignores Proactive posture (hardcoded trigger.expect)

findings.description: Line 36 hardcodes name="trigger.expect" while the sibling DeploymentStatusTriggerFields (same diff, line 31) and pre-existing FlowRunStateTriggerFields switch to trigger.after when posture is Proactive. Same defect as work-pool but a separate file requiring its own fix: selecting "Stays in" writes the status to expect and leaves after undefined, so the saved automation does not express the user's stated intent.

findings.description: Line 78 uses parseInt(e.target.value) while all three sibling components use Number(...). Two consequences: (1) `biome ci` fails with lint/style/useNumberNamespace at work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx:78, breaking the CI Lint job; (2) clearing the Threshold input stores NaN in form state where siblings store 0, and parseInt("1e3")=1 vs Number("1e3")=1000.
findings.failureMode: CI Lint job fails; NaN written into controlled number input and form state.
findings.title: Threshold uses parseInt, yielding NaN where siblings yield 0

findings.description: String.prototype.split never returns an empty array, so `lines.length > 0` is always true and the `: undefined` branch is unreachable. Clearing the textarea stores expect:[""], and blank lines store empty event names.
findings.failureMode: Automation saved with an empty-string expected event name instead of no expect filter.
findings.title: Custom trigger textarea stores [""] instead of undefined when cleared

findings.description: All four new component files (custom-trigger-fields.tsx, deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx, work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx, work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx) ship with no co-located .test.tsx, unlike the sibling flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx they are modelled on. AGENTS.md rule 10 requires component.test.tsx in the same directory.

findings.title: New trigger field components lack co-located test files (AGENTS.md rule 10)

findings.description: The rename of `pageActionStack` to `trailingPageActionStack` replaced `pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews` in `updateToolbarLayout` with a second `browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews` instead. New buttons are created with `alpha = 0` in `updateActionStack`, and `updateToolbarLayout` is the only place that restores alpha to 1.0. Any button newly added to the trailing page action stack (e.g. reload/QR/reader controls inside the address bar) now stays at alpha 0 and is invisible.
findings.failureMode: Wrong identifier: duplicated browserActionStack, dropped trailingPageActionStack from alpha restore list
findings.title: Trailing page action buttons never faded in (browserActionStack duplicated)

findings.description: The leading constraint changed from `leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor` to `rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor`, so with swiping tabs enabled both toolbar edges are tied to the right skeleton bar. The right skeleton's leading is at the container's trailing edge and its width is (container width - skeletonBarWidthOffset), so toolbar.leading resolves far to the right of toolbar.trailing, giving the toolbar a negative width: Auto Layout conflicts are logged and the address toolbar is not laid out correctly (URL bar collapsed). Reachable whenever the swipingTabs Nimbus flag is on (covered by SwipingTabsTests).
findings.failureMode: Wrong identifier in constraint: left skeleton replaced by right skeleton
findings.title: Toolbar leading anchor pinned to right skeleton bar, collapsing the address bar

findings.description: `hasPageActions` was `!pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.isEmpty` (the trailing stack); after the rename it reads `leadingPageActionStack`. `locationDividerView` is constrained to `trailingPageActionStack.leadingAnchor`, so its width must track the trailing stack. With trailing page actions present and no leading page actions (a common state, leadingPageActions is empty in many AddressBarState cases), the divider collapses to 0 and disappears; with leading actions but no trailing actions a divider is drawn next to nothing.
findings.failureMode: Wrong identifier substituted during rename, changing which stack drives the divider constraint
findings.title: Divider width now keyed off leading instead of trailing page actions

findings.description: `setupSkeletonAddressBarsLayout` gains `let isLandscape = UIApplication.shared.statusBarOrientation.isLandscape` plus a comment claiming layout adjustments, but the value is never read and no constraint depends on orientation. This produces compiler warnings in the Client build (unused immutable value, and `statusBarOrientation` deprecated since iOS 13 — the only remaining use of that API in the repo) and leaves a comment describing behaviour the code does not implement.
findings.failureMode: Dead code introducing build warnings and a comment that misstates behaviour
findings.title: Unused isLandscape local using deprecated statusBarOrientation

findings.description: The guard only rejects non-str values that are not None, so `rendered` stays `str | None` and `return rendered` violates the declared `-> str`. basedpyright (strict, run by CI `dev/basedpyright-check` and `make type-check`) reports reportReturnType on this line; the base file is clean.
findings.failureMode: CI type-check failure; latent TypeError in _run when result lacks "result"
findings.title: render_template can return None, breaking its `-> str` contract and failing basedpyright

findings.description: `assert "1, two, 3.0, True" == result.outputs["output"]` trips SIM300, which the repo's .ruff.toml selects. `ruff check ./api` (make check) exits 1 on this added line; the base file passed.
findings.failureMode: ruff check exits non-zero (mandate 2)
findings.title: New assertion fails ruff check (SIM300 yoda-condition)

findings.description: The removed line `keyword_like_val = f"%{keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')}%".replace(r"\u", r"\\u")` converted the keyword into the \uXXXX form actually stored in workflow_runs.inputs/outputs (written with json.dumps default ensure_ascii=True). The new pattern uses the raw keyword, so CJK/non-ASCII searches match nothing.
findings.failureMode: search returns zero results for non-ASCII keywords
findings.title: Workflow log keyword search breaks for non-ASCII keywords

findings.description: escape_like_pattern() prefixes % / _ / \ with a backslash, but the new SQL declares ESCAPE '|'. Backslash is then just a literal character while % and _ stay wildcards: a search for "50%" becomes pattern %50\%% and matches only text containing "50\", returning no rows; a query containing '|' has its next char un-wildcarded, returning false positives. Reachable when IRIS is the vector store and IRIS_TEXT_INDEX is set to false (default true).
findings.failureMode: wrong query results on IRIS LIKE fallback search
findings.title: IRIS LIKE fallback declares ESCAPE '|' while the pattern is backslash-escaped

findings.description: `escapedPattern` in the new escape_like_pattern helper is camelCase; repository rule 16 requires snake_case for Python variables (ruff N806 is disabled, so lint will not catch it).
findings.failureMode: repository naming mandate violation
findings.title: camelCase local variable violates snake_case mandate

findings.description: `rendered = result.get("result")` may be None; the guard only rejects non-str non-None values, so `return rendered` returns `str | None` from a function declared `-> str`. basedpyright (strict, run by the required Style check job) errors here.
findings.failureMode: CI type-check failure; None propagates to len() in _run
findings.title: render_template can return None, failing basedpyright and risking TypeError

findings.description: `assert "1, two, 3.0, True" == result.outputs["output"]` is a Yoda condition; `ruff check ./api` exits non-zero with SIM300 on this newly added line.
findings.failureMode: ruff check fails (mandate 2 / pre-commit hook)
findings.title: ruff check error SIM300 on added assertion
